==> .github/workflows/deploy.yml <==
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true
  TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '11.0.x'

      - name: Restore
        run: dotnet restore

      - name: Process content
        run: dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor --no-restore

      - name: Restore audio cache
        id: audio-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .audio-cache
          key: audio-v1-${{ hashFiles('content/blog/**/*.md') }}
          restore-keys: |
            audio-v1-

      - name: Copy cached audio to output
        run: |
          mkdir -p src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data
          shopt -s nullglob
          files=(.audio-cache/*.mp3 .audio-cache/audio-manifest.json)
          if (( ${#files[@]} )); then cp "${files[@]}" src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/; fi
          echo "Restored ${#files[@]} cached audio file(s)"

      - name: Setup Python
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: tools/requirements-audio.txt

      - name: Install system dependencies
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y espeak-ng ffmpeg

      - name: Cache Hugging Face model
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/huggingface
          key: hf-kitten-tts-nano-0.8

      - name: Install Python audio dependencies
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: pip install onnxruntime -r tools/requirements-audio.txt

      - name: Generate TTS audio
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: python tools/generate_audio.py --content-dir content/blog --output-dir src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data --voice Bella --model KittenML/kitten-tts-nano-0.8

      - name: Update audio cache
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p .audio-cache
          shopt -s nullglob
          files=(src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/*.mp3 src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/audio-manifest.json)
          if (( ${#files[@]} )); then cp "${files[@]}" .audio-cache/; fi
          echo "Cached ${#files[@]} audio file(s)"

      - name: Test
        run: dotnet test --solution ObserverMagazine.slnx --no-restore

      - name: Publish
        run: dotnet publish src/ObserverMagazine.Web/ObserverMagazine.Web.csproj -c Release -o publish

      - name: Prepare site
        run: cp publish/wwwroot/index.html publish/wwwroot/404.html

      - name: Setup Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: publish/wwwroot

      - name: Deploy
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

==> README.md <==
# Terlingua Magazine

A free, open-source Blazor WebAssembly application deployed to GitHub Pages.

Built with **.NET 11** and **C# 15**. Targets the current stable releases of evergreen browsers only
(Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari); there are no polyfills, vendor prefixes or legacy fallbacks.
Other browsers get an explicit error instead of a page stuck on loading (see
[Unsupported browsers](#unsupported-browsers)).

## Features

- **Blog** — Write posts in Markdown with YAML front matter; compiled to static JSON at build time
- **RSS Feed** — Auto-generated `feed.xml`
- **Books & Quizzes** — Multi-chapter books with single- and multiple-answer quizzes; reading progress stored in the browser (localStorage)
- **Responsive Tables** — Sortable, filterable data tables that work on mobile
- **Master-Detail Flow** — Click a list item to view full details
- **OpenTelemetry-ready Logging** — Structured logging via `ILogger`
- **Full Test Suite** — bUnit component tests + xUnit.net v3 integration tests, running on Microsoft.Testing.Platform

## Quick Start

`global.json` asks for SDK `11.0.100-rc.3` or any later 11.0.1xx SDK, so the Fedora RC 3 SDK works
locally and CI uses the latest .NET 11 GA SDK.

```bash
# Process blog posts and books
dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor

# Run the app locally
dotnet run --project src/ObserverMagazine.Web

# Run all tests
dotnet test
```

## Books

Books live under `content/books/` and are compiled by the content processor into
`wwwroot/book-data/` (git-ignored) at build time.

```
content/books/
  blazor-basics/                  # book slug (lowercase, digits, hyphens)
    book.yml                      # title, author, summary, date, tags, image, draft
    01-getting-started/           # NN-chapter-slug; the number sets the order
      chapter.yml                 # title, summary, draft
      01-what-is-blazor.md        # NN-subchapter-slug.md
      02-project-structure.md
    02-components/
      ...
```

Chapters and subchapters are numbered 1, 2, 3… in the order of their prefixes, so gaps
(`01`, `05`, `10`) are fine. Drafts and future-dated books are skipped.

### Subchapter format

```markdown
---
title: What is Blazor WebAssembly?
questions:
  - id: runtime                   # optional, defaults to q1, q2…; keep stable once published
    prompt: Where does the C# code run?
    explanation: Shown after a correct answer.   # optional
    options:
      - text: On the server
      - text: In the browser
        correct: true
  - id: hosting
    prompt: Which statements are true?
    type: multiple                # optional: single | multiple
    options:
      - id: static                # optional, defaults to a, b, c…
        text: It can be served from GitHub Pages
        correct: true
      - text: It needs ASP.NET Core on the server
---
Markdown body…
```

- `type` is inferred when omitted: more than one correct option means `multiple`.
  Set `type: multiple` explicitly to use checkboxes even when only one option is correct.
- Prompts, options and explanations support Markdown (inline code, emphasis, links).
- Question and option ids are what reader progress is keyed on. Changing them resets
  progress for that question.
- Invalid content (no correct option, fewer than two options, unnumbered files, missing
  `chapter.yml`, bad YAML, duplicate ids) fails the build with a list of errors.

Content guidelines for new sections:

- Open with a "Learning objectives" list and keep each section focused on one concept
- Prefer small, compilable code snippets with a language on every code fence
- Write three or more questions per section, mixing single- and multiple-answer questions,
  with an `explanation` on every question
- Vary the position of the correct option; the UI does not shuffle options
- Companions to published books follow the original chapter and section order, quote only short passages, and put each quotation inside “ ” in the `explanation` so it can be checked against the source
- Non-software books may grade claims by certainty; `nutrition-science` uses Established, Strong, Uncertain and Not supported, and cites sources at the end of each section
- Quote option text that YAML would read as a boolean, number or null (`"Yes"`, `"50"`), and avoid `yes`, `no`, `null`, `true` and `false` as ids
- Quote YAML values that contain `: `, ` #` or start with a backtick or `@`

### Progress and analytics

- A section is complete when every question has been answered correctly, or, if it has
  no questions, once it has been opened.
- Progress is saved per book in `localStorage` under `book:<slug>`. If storage is
  unavailable (blocked storage, quota) the app falls back to in-memory storage and tells
  the reader that progress will not persist.
- When the analytics backend is reachable, the reader count of a book and of each
  section is shown. A reader is counted once per book and once per section, using the
  local progress record to avoid counting repeat visits. Quiz answers are sent as
  interaction events. Nothing is shown and nothing breaks when the backend is down.

## Front end

- The site ships no JavaScript of its own apart from the inline boot-failure reporter in
  `index.html` (see [Unsupported browsers](#unsupported-browsers)). The only interop is
  `localStorage` through `LocalBrowserStorage` (`IBrowserStorage`), which wraps every call in
  `try`/`catch` as analyzer BL0016 requires.
- Code blocks are highlighted at build time by `SyntaxHighlighter` in the content processor,
  plugged into Markdig as `SyntaxHighlightingExtension`. The `hl-*` colour classes live in
  `app.css`.
- Horizontally scrolling code blocks show edge shadows with pure CSS
  (`background-attachment: local`).
- Themes are CSS custom properties. `MainLayout` renders `data-theme` on `.page` and saves the
  choice in `localStorage` (`observer-theme`). The default `system` theme uses `light-dark()`
  and `color-scheme`, so it follows the OS setting live. The loading screen always uses the
  system theme.
- The audio player uses the browser's native controls, including playback speed, and stays
  hidden until the MP3's metadata loads.
- `OverrideHtmlAssetPlaceholders` fingerprints the framework files (`dotnet.js` is published as
  `dotnet.<hash>.js`) and fills the `<script type="importmap">` placeholder in `index.html`,
  which is how `blazor.webassembly.js` finds them. Keep that placeholder, and don't modify files
  under `_framework` after publish, because the import map can carry integrity hashes for them.
  A 404 for `/_framework/dotnet.js` on the live site is expected.
- GitHub Pages deep links work because CI copies the published `index.html` to `404.html`.

### Unsupported browsers

`index.html` makes the app fail loudly instead of leaving "Loading Terlingua Magazine…" on screen
forever. Both failure states use the `.app-failure` card in `app.css`, built from the same design
tokens as the rest of the site.

- **JavaScript off.** A `<noscript>` card inside `#app` says JavaScript is required, and a
  `<noscript>` style in `<head>` hides the loading text.
- **Boot failure.** An inline classic script, placed before `blazor.webassembly.js`, listens for
  `error` (capture phase) and `unhandledrejection`. On the first one it replaces the loading text
  with a copy of `<template id="boot-error-template">` and appends one line per error:
  `[unhandledrejection]` for rejected promises such as WebAssembly compile errors and runtime
  feature checks, `[error]` for script errors such as syntax the browser can't parse, and
  `[resource error]` for a `<script>` that fails to load. Other failed resources (stylesheets,
  images) are ignored because they don't stop the app.
- **After boot** the reporter does nothing: Blazor clears `#app` when it renders, so the loading
  text is gone and later errors go to `#blazor-error-ui` as before.
- The reporter is the one place where older browsers matter, because it has to run where the app
  can't. It uses ES2015 syntax and DOM APIs that any browser with WebAssembly support understands.
  It sets text with `textContent` only. Keep it before `blazor.webassembly.js` and keep it a
  classic script, not a module.
- `app.css` uses `light-dark()`, which these browsers ignore, so the card falls back to the
  browser's default colours. That is expected; it stays readable and needs no fallback.

Before, an iPhone 8 Plus or a Nexus 6 sat on the loading text with no explanation:

<img src="docs/images/nexus-6-loading.png" alt="Nexus 6 stuck on Loading Terlingua Magazine" width="240">

Now they report why the runtime can't start (no WebAssembly SIMD on the Nexus 6, no WebAssembly
exception handling on the iPhone 8 Plus):

<img src="docs/images/nexus-6-failed.png" alt="Nexus 6 boot failure: WASM SIMD not supported" width="240"> <img src="docs/images/iphone-eight-plus-failed.png" alt="iPhone 8 Plus boot failure: WASM exception handling not supported" width="240">

To check the boot-failure path locally, block `_framework/blazor.webassembly*.js` in the browser
dev tools' network panel and reload; the card shows a `[resource error]` line. To check the
no-JavaScript path, turn JavaScript off for the site and reload.

## Testing

Tests run on **Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP)**, not VSTest. The opt-in lives in
`global.json`:

```json
{ "test": { "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform" } }
```

Test projects are ordinary executables, so each one can also be run on its own:

```bash
# Whole solution
dotnet test --solution ObserverMagazine.slnx

# One project
dotnet test --project tests/ObserverMagazine.Web.Tests

# Filter by class, or by trait
dotnet test --filter-class ObserverMagazine.Web.Tests.Services.BlogServiceTests
dotnet test --filter-trait Category=Integration

# Run a test project directly, no dotnet test involved
dotnet run --project tests/ObserverMagazine.Integration.Tests
```

Run `dotnet test -?` from the repo root for the full option list, which is built
from whichever MTP extensions the test projects reference.

xUnit configuration for MTP lives in `testconfig.json` next to a test project
(not `xunit.runner.json`, which is the VSTest-era file).

## LLM context export

`export.sh` writes `docs/llm/dump.txt`, a single-file snapshot of the repository for LLM
project knowledge. To keep it small it includes full text only for source, config and docs.
Blog posts contribute front matter, books one inventory line each (the book format is
documented above), and binary and data files (`wwwroot/plaintext/`) their path. `docs/` is
never exported. The script prints the dump's size and largest files when it finishes.

```bash
bash export.sh                                   # whole repository
bash export.sh -- ':!tests' ':!*Showcase*'       # narrow with git pathspecs
bash export.sh -f -o /tmp/dapper.txt -- content/books/dapper   # full text of one book
```

# NOTES — data-representation-traps

Decisions and conflicts, logged as the build proceeds. Source-of-truth order: compiler source > existing books > prompt.

## Repository facts learned (Step 0)

- `dump.txt` (project doc) read first; full repo cloned read-only from `github.com/terlingua/terlingua.github.io` at commit `033766a2` (2026-11-27) to read existing books. Only files under `content/books/data-representation-traps/` and `_build/data-representation-traps/` are created.
- Author id: `terlingua-team` exists in `content/authors/terlingua-team.yml` → used.
- Date format in existing `book.yml`: unquoted `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `date: 2026-11-10`). Used `date: 2026-11-27`. `BookManifest.Date` is `DateTime`; YamlDotNet parses the plain scalar. A quoted date would also parse, but unquoted matches existing books.
- `publishBefore` defaults to `DateTime.UtcNow`; `2026-11-27` (midnight) is not in the future on the build day, so the book is not skipped.
- Naming: `ContentNaming` regexes — book slug `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`; numbered entries `^(\d+)[-_]([a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*)$`. Files/folders starting with `.` or `_` are hidden (ignored).
- YAML keys: camelCase naming convention, unmatched properties ignored. Book: `title` (required), `author`, `summary`, `date`, `updated`, `tags`, `image`, `draft`. Chapter: `title` (required), `summary`, `draft`. Subchapter: `title` (required), `draft`, `questions`.
- Questions (`QuestionCompiler`): `id` optional (defaults `q1`…) but must match slug regex and be unique; `prompt` required; `type` optional: `single` | `multiple` (case-insensitive after trim); unknown type = error; `single` with >1 correct = error; ≥2 options; ≥1 correct. Option `id` optional (defaults `a`, `b`, …), `text` required, `correct` is a YAML bool (missing = false).
- `explanation` optional in the compiler; the prompt makes it mandatory → stricter rule applied.
- Front matter delimiter: content must start with `---`; the block ends at the FIRST occurrence of `\n---` anywhere after it. Therefore no line inside front matter may start with `---` (indented lines inside block scalars are safe). The body is everything after.
- Code fences: `SyntaxHighlighter` handles `csharp`(`cs`), `javascript`(`js`), `typescript`(`ts`), `python`, `sql`, `bash`(`sh`,`shell`,`zsh`), `json`, `yaml`(`yml`), `html`(`xml`), `css`. Intersection with the prompt's set = all eight of `csharp python javascript sql bash json yaml html`. Unknown languages would still render (plain), but are disallowed by the validator.

## Conflicts and resolutions

1. **Block scalars.** Existing books never use `explanation: |-` (59 files use folded `>`). YamlDotNet supports literal block scalars (YAML 1.1/1.2 core syntax), so `|-` is accepted by the compiler; prompt prefers it → used `|-` for every explanation.
2. **Real compiler not runnable.** The sandbox cannot reach `dot.net`, `builds.dotnet.microsoft.com` or `api.nuget.org` (proxy 403), so the .NET 11 SDK and the Markdig/YamlDotNet packages cannot be installed; `dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor` was not possible. Mitigation: `validate.py` contains a faithful Python port of `FrontMatterParser.Parse` (delimiter logic), `ContentNaming`, `BookCompiler` (manifest/title/draft/numbering/duplicate checks) and `QuestionCompiler` (ids, options, correct counts, type resolution), parsed with PyYAML (YAML 1.1, which is stricter than YamlDotNet about booleans — every string is double-quoted, so the difference cannot bite). The author should run `dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor` once locally; see REPORT.md.
3. **`draft: false`.** Existing book.yml files omit `draft`; the prompt requires `draft: false`. Harmless (default false) → included.
4. **`type` required by prompt, optional in compiler** → always written.
5. **Answer positions.** The prompt's formula is applied mechanically by `normalize.py`: options are authored in any order, then the script moves correct options to index `(k + s) mod n` (and the following indexes, wrapping, for `multiple`) while keeping distractors in authored order. Explanations never reference positions, so reordering is safe. `s` is the 1-based section number across the whole book (1–28).
6. **The 40% rule** is checked over all correct options (including every correct option of `multiple` questions) per section, and also over first-correct positions.
7. **Book `summary`/`title`** taken verbatim from the prompt.
8. **Section count:** 28 (4+5+4+4+4+4+3).

## Dated-claim verification log (all checked 2026-11-27)

- Unicode: `unicode.org/versions/latest` redirects to `Unicode18.0.0`; Unicode 18.0 released September 2026 (planned 15 Sept 2026 per unicode.org beta page; GCC libstdc++ patch dated 17 Sept 2026 updates to 18.0.0). Character totals differ between sources (13,047 vs 13,007 new) → no counts stated.
- CGPM: 28th CGPM (13–15 Oct 2026) adopted Resolution 5 "On the technical actions needed to ensure the continuity of UTC" (listed on bipm.org/en/cgpm-2026). Draft Resolution C text (bipm.org): continuous UTC effective 20 May 2027; max |UT1−UTC| = 3 600 s. 27th CGPM (2022) Resolution 4 is the earlier "in, or before, 2035" decision.
- IERS Bulletin C 72 (6 Jul 2026): no leap second end of December 2026; UTC−TAI = −37 s since 2017-01-01.
- Temporal: reached TC39 Stage 4 at the March 2026 plenary (Igalia announcement 2026-03-13; proposal README says Stage 4). Which ECMAScript edition includes it is reported inconsistently → not stated.
- MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: `utf8` is a deprecated alias for `utf8mb3`; `utf8mb3` is BMP-only, max 3 bytes, deprecated; `utf8mb4` recommended. `TIMESTAMP` range '1970-01-01 00:00:01' UTC to '2038-01-19 03:14:07' UTC.
- Python 3.12 What's New: `sum()` uses Neumaier summation for floats.
- glibc 2.34: `_TIME_BITS=64` (with `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64`) gives 64-bit `time_t` on 32-bit Linux ABIs.
- IEEE P3109 (Arithmetic Formats for Machine Learning): still a draft / active PAR (interim report v4.0 dated June 2026). OCP MX specification v1.1 dated October 2026. OCP FP8 E4M3/E5M2 layouts from the OCP 8-bit floating point spec.
- Not stated because unverifiable or volatile: specific browser versions shipping Temporal, Linux kernel version numbers, current tzdata release name, NumPy internals beyond "pairwise".

## Section-level decisions

- Product facts used only in "Where this shows up today" or labeled vendor-specific; no answer depends solely on a dated fact. Questions that touch vendor behavior (e.g. MySQL `utf8mb3`) are explained from the invariant (4-byte UTF-8 for astral code points).

## Decisions made while writing (chronological)

- **Write-tool escape hazard.** Escapes such as `́` and `‍` typed into files were turned into the literal characters by the file-writing tool (seen in s=12, s=14, s=15). Fixed each case, then added guards: `normalize.py` rejects format, control, private-use, surrogate and combining characters (Cf/Cc/Co/Cs/Mn/Me) in YAML strings, and `validate.py` rejects them in bodies. Code samples now use `chr(0x301)` or explicit `"́"` escapes that were verified on disk.
- **ZWJ emoji are never written literally** (they contain U+200D); they are described by code points instead.
- **Markdig emphasis extras.** `MarkdownProcessor` uses `UseAdvancedExtensions()`, which enables `^superscript^` and `==mark==`. Prose such as "2^−126 … 2^−149" or "x == y … x == y" in one paragraph would render as superscript/highlight. `normalize.py` therefore escapes `^` as `\^` and `==` as `\==` outside code spans and fences in bodies, prompts, options and explanations (titles and chapter summaries are plain text and left alone). Checked that no `$`, `~`, `++`, `{`, `[^` or definition-list `: ` lines occur outside code.
- **Table pipes.** A `|` inside a table cell (bitwise OR in the UTF-16 decode formula) broke a table in s=13; rewrote the formula with `+`. A table-shape check found no other issues.
- **Mix rules per section** (≥2 compute/trace, ≥1 spot-the-bug/what-prints) were checked by hand; s=4 and s=18 lacked a what-prints question, so their first/second questions were rewritten as code-output questions (Python `struct` decoding of `0xFF800000`; JavaScript `| 0` int32 wrap).
- **Correct-answer length.** validate.py fails a section if the correct option is the unique longest in more than half of its single-answer questions (book-wide limit 40%); several option sets were rebalanced. Final: 21 of 141.
- **Explanation quotes** were normalized (fix_quotes.py) so every distractor is referred to by its exact option text; audit.py's remaining 16 hits are verified false positives (prefix matches such as "Plane 15" vs "Plane 1", or explanations that discuss a distractor inside a sentence instead of quoting it).
- **Dated questions** (at most one per section): s=4 OCP FP8 details, s=9 ISO 4217 exponents, s=13 MySQL 8.4 `utf8`, s=18 MySQL 8.4 `TIMESTAMP`, s=20 CGPM 2026 Resolution 5, s=24 tzdata packaging. Each explanation states the timeless rule that also justifies the answer.
- **Removed unverified version claims**: NumPy's pairwise-summation start version (not confirmed in primary sources) was replaced by a reference to the current NumPy documentation; exact Unicode 18.0 character counts omitted; ECMAScript edition containing Temporal omitted.
- **Plan deviations**: s=5 replaced "shortest round-trip printing" (covered in s=2) with a float-literal-versus-double question; s=13 has 7 questions; s=25 uses 2027-01-01 (week-year 2026-W53) for the ISO week question because it exposes the `%Y`/`%G` trap; s=18's wraparound question became a JavaScript `| 0` question.

## Unresolved uncertainties and how they were handled

- **Not verifiable / dropped:** the ECMAScript edition that contains Temporal (sources disagree); exact Unicode 18.0 character totals (13,047 vs 13,007); the NumPy version that introduced pairwise summation; specific browser versions. These are stated generically or omitted.
- **Stated from long-standing documentation without a fresh fetch:** .NET behaviors (`Math.Round` half-even default, `AddYears` clamping, `ToUpperInvariant` simple case mapping, `Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime` in .NET 7+, `TimeProvider` in .NET 8, IANA IDs on all platforms since .NET 6), PostgreSQL `timestamptz` semantics, SQL Server `varchar`/`nvarchar` length units, RFC 3339 `-00:00` semantics and lowercase `t`/`z`, RFC 2781 big-endian default, UTS #39 skeleton guidance. All are vendor-labeled in the text; none is the sole basis of an answer.
- **C# snippets were not executed** (no .NET SDK); their outputs were reasoned from documented behavior and, where possible, cross-checked by computing the same values in Python.
- **Markdig rendering** was not executed; escaping of `^` and `==` was added defensively because `UseAdvancedExtensions()` enables superscript and mark syntax.

==> _build/data-representation-traps/audit.py <==
import re
import yaml
from common import sections, split_front_matter


def norm(t):
    t = t.replace("`", "").replace("\\", "")
    t = re.sub(r"[\s\.\,;:!?\"']+", " ", t).strip().lower()
    return t


def main():
    problems = 0
    for s, (_, path) in enumerate(sections(), start=1):
        fm = yaml.safe_load(split_front_matter(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())[0])
        for k, q in enumerate(fm["questions"], start=1):
            loc = f"s={s} {q['id']}"
            expl = q["explanation"]
            quoted = [norm(m) for m in re.findall(r'^\s*(?:- )?"(.+?)"(?= )', expl, flags=re.M)]
            wrong_section = expl.split("Wrong:")[1] if "Wrong:" in expl else expl
            for o in q["options"]:
                t = norm(o["text"])
                hits = [x for x in quoted if x and (t.startswith(x) or x.startswith(t))]
                if o.get("correct"):
                    if hits and q["type"] == "single":
                        print(f"{loc}: correct option quoted like a distractor: {o['text']}")
                        problems += 1
                else:
                    mentioned = hits or t[:25] in norm(wrong_section)
                    if not mentioned:
                        print(f"{loc}: distractor not addressed in explanation: {o['text']}")
                        problems += 1
            if q["type"] == "multiple":
                if "Correct:" not in expl or "Wrong:" not in expl:
                    print(f"{loc}: multiple question lacks Correct:/Wrong: structure")
                    problems += 1
                else:
                    corr_part = expl.split("Wrong:")[0]
                    for o in q["options"]:
                        if not o.get("correct") and norm(o["text"])[:30] in norm(corr_part) and norm(o["text"])[:30] not in norm(wrong_section):
                            print(f"{loc}: wrong option appears only in the Correct part: {o['text']}")
                            problems += 1
    print(f"audit: {problems} potential problem(s)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> _build/data-representation-traps/check_math.py <==
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import struct, math, unicodedata, datetime, calendar
from decimal import Decimal
from fractions import Fraction

checks = 0
def ok(cond, label):
    global checks
    checks += 1
    if not cond:
        raise AssertionError(label)

def f32_bits(x): return struct.unpack(">I", struct.pack(">f", x))[0]
def f64_bits(x): return struct.unpack(">Q", struct.pack(">d", x))[0]
def bits_f32(b): return struct.unpack(">f", struct.pack(">I", b))[0]
def bits_f64(b): return struct.unpack(">d", struct.pack(">Q", b))[0]
def s32(u): return u - (1 << 32) if u & 0x80000000 else u

# s=1 three fields and the bias
ok(2**(8-1)-1 == 127 and 2**(11-1)-1 == 1023, "biases")
ok(f32_bits(32.0) == 0x42000000 and (0x42000000 >> 23) & 0xFF == 132, "32.0f")
ok(f32_bits(1.0) == 0x3F800000, "1.0f")
ok(f64_bits(1.0) == 0x3FF0000000000000, "1.0")
ok(f64_bits(2.0) == 0x4000000000000000, "2.0")
ok(f64_bits(32.0) == 0x4040000000000000 and (0x4040000000000000 >> 52) == 1028, "32.0 double")
ok(f32_bits(2.5) == 0x40200000 and bits_f32(0x40200000 ^ 0x80000000) == -2.5, "xor sign")
ok(s32(0xC0200000) == -1071644672, "reinterpreted int")
ok(s32(f32_bits(-1.0)) == -1082130432 and s32(f32_bits(-2.0)) == -1073741824, "neg sort")
ok(f32_bits(-2.5) == 0xC0200000 and f64_bits(-2.5) == 0xC004000000000000, "-2.5")
ok(bits_f64(1) == 2**-1074 and str(Decimal(2**-1074))[:4] == "4.94", "min subnormal double")

# s=2 hidden bit
ok(f32_bits(-6.5) == 0xC0D00000 and bits_f32(0xC0E80000) == -7.25 and bits_f32(0xC0500000) == -3.25, "-6.5")
ok(bits_f32(0x3E200000) == 0.15625 and bits_f32(0x3EA00000) == 0.3125, "0x3E200000")
ok(Decimal(bits_f32(0x40490FDB)) == Decimal("3.1415927410125732421875"), "float pi exact")
ok(Fraction(bits_f32(0x40490FDB)) == Fraction(13176795, 4194304), "float pi fraction")
ok(abs((bits_f32(0x40490FDB) - math.pi) - 8.74e-8) < 1e-9, "float pi error")
ok(repr(bits_f32(0x40490FDB)) == "3.1415927410125732", "repr widened")
ok(((0x40000000 >> 23) & 0x7F) - 127 == -127 and ((0x3F800000 >> 23) & 0x7F) - 127 == 0, "mask bug")
ok(bits_f32(0x7F7FFFFF) == (2 - 2**-23) * 2**127 == 2**128 - 2**104, "max float")
ok(bits_f32(0x7F800000) == math.inf, "inf")
ok(round(53 * math.log10(2), 2) == 15.95, "digits")

# s=3 subnormals
import numpy as np
ok(bits_f32(0x00800000) == 2.0**-126 and bits_f32(0x00000001) == 2.0**-149, "min normal/subnormal f32")
ok(bits_f32(0x00200000) == 2.0**-128, "2^-128 pattern")
ok(bits_f32(0x00000003) == 3 * 2.0**-149, "0x3 subnormal")
ok(5e-324 == 2.0**-1074 and 5e-324 / 2 == 0.0 and 5e-324 * 0.75 == 5e-324, "underflow print")
a32, b32 = np.float32(1.5e-38), np.float32(1.2e-38)
ok(a32 >= np.float32(2.0**-126) and b32 >= np.float32(2.0**-126), "inputs normal")
d32 = a32 - b32
ok(0 < d32 < np.float32(2.0**-126), "difference subnormal")
ok(abs(float(np.float32(1) / d32) - 3.33e38) / 3.33e38 < 0.01 and np.isfinite(np.float32(1) / d32), "reciprocal finite")
ok(2.0**-1022 == 2.2250738585072014e-308, "min normal f64")
ok(np.finfo(np.float32).smallest_subnormal == np.float32(2.0**-149), "float.Epsilon")

# s=4 special encodings
ok(math.isinf(bits_f32(0xFF800000)) and bits_f32(0xFF800000) < 0, "-inf")
ok(bits_f32(0xFF7FFFFF) == -bits_f32(0x7F7FFFFF), "most negative finite")
b = 0x7FA00000
ok((b >> 23) & 0xFF == 0xFF and b & 0x7FFFFF != 0 and not (b >> 22) & 1, "signaling NaN")
ok((0x7FC00000 >> 22) & 1 == 1, "quiet NaN bit")
ok(2 * (2**23 - 1) == 2**24 - 2 == 16777214, "NaN count")
ok((2 - 2**-10) * 2**15 == 65504 and float(np.frombuffer(bytes.fromhex("7bff")[::-1], dtype=np.float16)[0]) == 65504, "binary16 max")
ok(np.isinf(np.frombuffer(bytes.fromhex("7c00")[::-1], dtype=np.float16)[0]), "binary16 inf")
ok(np.isinf(np.float16(65520.0)) and float(np.float16(65504.0)) == 65504.0, "65520 overflows")
ok(bits_f32(0x40490000) == 3.140625 and 0x0FDB < 0x8000, "bfloat16 pi")
ok(bits_f32(0x40480000) == 3.125, "3.125 distractor")
ok((2 - 2**-7) * 2**127 > 3.38e38 and (2 - 2**-7) * 2**127 < 3.40e38, "bfloat16 max")

# s=7 cancellation

ok(-_b + _d == -2**-26 and -_b - _d == -2e8, "quadratic numerators")
def _kahan(xs):
    s = c = 0.0
    for x in xs:
        y = x - c; t = s + y; c = (t - s) - y; s = t
    return s
_n = 0.0
for _x in [1e16, 1.0, 1.0]:
    _n += _x
ok(_n == 1e16 and repr(_kahan([1e16, 1.0, 1.0])) == "1.0000000000000002e+16", "kahan")
ok(math.fsum([1e16, 1.0, 1.0]) == 1e16 + 2, "fsum")

# s=19 leap years

def _trunc(data, limit):
    if len(data) <= limit:
        return data
    cut = limit
    while cut > 0 and (data[cut] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        cut -= 1
    return data[:cut]

==> _build/data-representation-traps/common.py <==
import os
import re

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", ".."))
BOOK = os.path.join(ROOT, "content", "books", "data-representation-traps")

NUMBERED = re.compile(r"^(\d+)[-_]([a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*)$")
SLUG = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$")


def hidden(name):
    return name.startswith(".") or name.startswith("_")


def numbered(entries):
    out = []
    for path in entries:
        name = os.path.basename(path)
        if name.endswith(".md"):
            name = name[:-3]
        m = NUMBERED.match(name)
        out.append((int(m.group(1)) if m else -1, m.group(2) if m else None, path))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda e: (e[0], e[2]))


def chapters():
    dirs = [os.path.join(BOOK, d) for d in os.listdir(BOOK)
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(BOOK, d)) and not hidden(d)]
    return numbered(dirs)


def sections():
    result = []
    for _, _, cdir in chapters():
        files = [os.path.join(cdir, f) for f in os.listdir(cdir)
                 if f.endswith(".md") and not hidden(f)]
        for entry in numbered(files):
            result.append((cdir, entry[2]))
    return result


def split_front_matter(raw):
    if not raw.startswith("---"):
        return None, raw
    end = raw.find("\n---", 3)
    if end < 0:
        return None, raw
    yaml_block = raw[3:end].strip()
    body = raw[end + 4:].lstrip("\r\n")
    return yaml_block, body

==> _build/data-representation-traps/fix_quotes.py <==
import re, difflib, yaml
from common import sections, split_front_matter

def key(t):
    return re.sub(r"[`\\]", "", t).rstrip(".").strip()

changed = 0
for s, (_, path) in enumerate(sections(), 1):
    raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    yb, body = split_front_matter(raw)
    fm = yaml.safe_load(yb)
    new_raw = raw
    for q in fm["questions"]:
        distractors = [o["text"] for o in q["options"] if not o.get("correct")]
        expl = q["explanation"]
        new_expl = expl
        for m in re.finditer(r'^(\s*(?:- )?)"(.+?)"(?= )', expl, flags=re.M):
            quoted = m.group(2)
            best, score = None, 0
            for d in distractors:
                r = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, key(quoted).lower(), key(d).lower()).ratio()
                if r > score:
                    best, score = d, r
            target = best.rstrip(".") if best else None
            if best and score >= 0.55 and quoted != target:
                new_expl = new_expl.replace(f'"{quoted}"', f'"{target}"', 1)
                print(f"s={s} {q['id']}: {quoted!r} -> {target!r} ({score:.2f})")
        if new_expl != expl:
            old_block = "\n".join(("      " + l) if l.strip() else "" for l in expl.split("\n"))
            new_block = "\n".join(("      " + l) if l.strip() else "" for l in new_expl.split("\n"))
            assert old_block in new_raw, q["id"]
            new_raw = new_raw.replace(old_block, new_block, 1)
            changed += 1
    if new_raw != raw:
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(new_raw)
print("questions changed:", changed)

==> _build/data-representation-traps/normalize.py <==
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
import yaml
from common import sections, split_front_matter

INDENT_EXPL = "      "


def dq(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise ValueError(f"expected string, got {value!r}")
    for ch in value:
        if ch in "\r\t":
            raise ValueError(f"control character in {value!r}")
        if ch != "\n" and unicodedata.category(ch) in ("Cf", "Cc", "Co", "Cs", "Mn", "Me"):
            raise ValueError(f"invisible/format character U+{ord(ch):04X} in {value!r}")
    return '"' + value.strip("\n").replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'


def block(value):
    lines = value.strip("\n").split("\n")
    if lines[0].startswith(" "):
        raise ValueError("explanation must not start with a space")
    for line in lines:
        for ch in line:
            if unicodedata.category(ch) in ("Cf", "Cc", "Co", "Cs", "Mn", "Me") and ch != "\t":
                raise ValueError(f"invisible character U+{ord(ch):04X} in explanation")
        if line.startswith("---"):
            raise ValueError("line starting with --- in explanation")
    return "|-\n" + "\n".join((INDENT_EXPL + l.rstrip()) if l.strip() else "" for l in lines)


CODE = re.compile(r"```.*?```|`[^`\n]*`", re.S)


def escape_md(text):
    """Escape Markdig emphasis-extra delimiters (^ superscript, == mark) outside code."""
    out, pos = [], 0
    for m in CODE.finditer(text):
        out.append(_esc(text[pos:m.start()]))
        out.append(m.group(0))
        pos = m.end()
    out.append(_esc(text[pos:]))
    return "".join(out)


def _esc(t):
    t = re.sub(r"(?<!\\)\^", r"\\^", t)
    t = re.sub(r"(?<![\\=])==", r"\\==", t)
    return t


def place(options, k, s):
    n = len(options)
    correct = [o for o in options if o.get("correct") is True]
    wrong = [o for o in options if o.get("correct") is not True]
    first = (k + s) % n
    targets = sorted((first + j) % n for j in range(len(correct)))
    out = [None] * n
    for t, o in zip(targets, correct):
        out[t] = o
    it = iter(wrong)
    for i in range(n):
        if out[i] is None:
            out[i] = next(it)
    return out


def emit(fm, body):
    lines = ["---", f"title: {dq(fm['title'])}", "questions:"]
    for q in fm["questions"]:
        lines.append(f"  - id: {dq(q['id'])}")
        lines.append(f"    type: {dq(q['type'])}")
        lines.append(f"    prompt: {dq(q['prompt'])}")
        lines.append(f"    explanation: {block(q['explanation'])}")
        lines.append("    options:")
        for o in q["options"]:
            lines.append(f"      - text: {dq(o['text'])}")
            if o.get("correct") is True:
                lines.append("        correct: true")
    lines.append("---")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n" + body.strip("\n") + "\n"


def main(only=None):
    for s, (_, path) in enumerate(sections(), start=1):
        if only and only not in path:
            continue
        raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        yb, body = split_front_matter(raw)
        fm = yaml.safe_load(yb)
        for k, q in enumerate(fm["questions"], start=1):
            q["options"] = place(q["options"], k, s)
            q["prompt"] = escape_md(q["prompt"])
            q["explanation"] = escape_md(q["explanation"])
            for o in q["options"]:
                o["text"] = escape_md(o["text"])
        body = escape_md(body)
        out = emit(fm, body)
        check = yaml.safe_load(split_front_matter(out)[0])
        assert check == fm, f"round-trip mismatch in {path}"
        if out != raw:
            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(out)
            print(f"normalized s={s} {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None)

==> _build/data-representation-traps/positions.py <==
import sys
from collections import Counter
s = int(sys.argv[1])
spec = sys.argv[2:]  # like 4 4 5:2 4 5:3
allc, first = Counter(), Counter()
tot = 0
for k, item in enumerate(spec, 1):
    n, c = (item.split(":") + ["1"])[:2]
    n, c = int(n), int(c)
    f = (k + s) % n
    first[f] += 1
    for j in range(c):
        allc[(f + j) % n] += 1
        tot += 1
    print(f"k={k} n={n} first={f}")
print("all", dict(allc), max(allc.values()) / tot, "first", dict(first), max(first.values()) / len(spec))

==> _build/data-representation-traps/validate.py <==
import os
import re
import sys
import datetime
from collections import Counter
import yaml
import unicodedata
from common import BOOK, SLUG, NUMBERED, hidden, chapters, sections, split_front_matter

ALLOWED_LANGS = {"csharp", "python", "javascript", "sql", "bash", "json", "yaml", "html"}
RESERVED_IDS = {"yes", "no", "true", "false", "null", "on", "off", "y", "n", "~"}
HEADINGS = ["Learning objectives", "The invariant", "Worked example",
            "Where this shows up today", "Pitfalls checklist", "Key takeaways"]
STRING_KEYS = ("title", "id", "prompt", "text", "type", "summary")

errors = []
warnings = []
stats = {"sections": 0, "questions": 0, "single": 0, "multiple": 0, "words": []}
longest_correct = [0, 0]


def err(loc, msg):
    errors.append(f"{loc}: {msg}")


def warn(loc, msg):
    warnings.append(f"{loc}: {msg}")


def rel(p):
    return os.path.relpath(p, os.path.dirname(BOOK))


def check_book():
    path = os.path.join(BOOK, "book.yml")
    raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    data = yaml.safe_load(raw)
    for key in ("title", "author", "summary", "date", "tags", "draft"):
        if key not in data:
            err(rel(path), f"missing {key}")
    if data.get("draft") is not False:
        err(rel(path), "draft must be false")
    if data.get("author") != "terlingua-team":
        err(rel(path), "author must be terlingua-team")
    if data.get("date") != datetime.date(2026, 11, 27):
        err(rel(path), f"date must be 2026-11-27, got {data.get('date')!r}")
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(BOOK, "..", "..", "authors", f"{data.get('author')}.yml")):
        err(rel(path), "author profile missing")
    if data.get("tags") != ["fundamentals", "floating-point", "unicode", "time", "engineering"]:
        err(rel(path), "tags mismatch")
    if not SLUG.match(os.path.basename(BOOK)):
        err(rel(BOOK), "bad book slug")


def check_chapter(cdir):
    name = os.path.basename(cdir)
    if not NUMBERED.match(name):
        err(rel(cdir), "bad chapter folder name")
    path = os.path.join(cdir, "chapter.yml")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        err(rel(cdir), "chapter.yml missing")
        return
    data = yaml.safe_load(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())
    for key in ("title", "summary", "draft"):
        if key not in data:
            err(rel(path), f"missing {key}")
    if data.get("draft") is not False:
        err(rel(path), "draft must be false")
    if not isinstance(data.get("title"), str) or not data["title"].strip():
        err(rel(path), "title required")


def raw_quote_checks(loc, yb):
    for i, line in enumerate(yb.split("\n"), start=1):
        if line.startswith("---"):
            err(loc, f"front matter line {i} starts with ---")
        m = re.match(r"^\s*(?:-\s+)?([a-zA-Z]+):\s*(.*)$", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if key in STRING_KEYS and not val.startswith('"'):
            err(loc, f"line {i}: {key} value must be double-quoted")
        if key == "explanation" and val != "|-":
            err(loc, f"line {i}: explanation must use |- block scalar")
        if key == "correct" and val != "true":
            err(loc, f"line {i}: correct must be 'true' when present")


def words(text):
    return len([w for w in re.split(r"\s+", text) if w])


def body_checks(loc, body):
    if not body.startswith("## Learning objectives"):
        err(loc, "body must start with '## Learning objectives'")
    heads = re.findall(r"^## (.+)$", body, flags=re.M)
    if heads != HEADINGS:
        err(loc, f"headings {heads} != {HEADINGS}")
    for m in re.finditer(r"^```(.*)$", body, flags=re.M):
        pass
    fences = re.findall(r"^```(\S*)\s*$", body, flags=re.M)
    if len(fences) % 2:
        err(loc, "unbalanced code fences")
    for i, lang in enumerate(fences):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            if not lang:
                err(loc, "code fence without language")
            elif lang not in ALLOWED_LANGS:
                err(loc, f"code fence language '{lang}' not allowed")
        elif lang:
            err(loc, "closing fence has text")
    parts = re.split(r"^## (.+)$", body, flags=re.M)
    sections_map = {parts[i]: parts[i + 1] for i in range(1, len(parts) - 1, 2)}

    def bullets(name):
        return len(re.findall(r"^- ", sections_map.get(name, ""), flags=re.M))

    for name, lo, hi in (("Learning objectives", 3, 5), ("Pitfalls checklist", 3, 6), ("Key takeaways", 3, 5)):
        n = bullets(name)
        if not lo <= n <= hi:
            err(loc, f"{name} has {n} bullets (want {lo}-{hi})")
    prose = re.sub(r"^```.*?^```", " ", body, flags=re.M | re.S)
    prose_no_tables = "\n".join(l for l in prose.split("\n") if not l.lstrip().startswith("|"))
    total = words(prose_no_tables)
    stats["words"].append(total)
    if not 400 <= total <= 1200:
        err(loc, f"prose word count {total} outside 400-1200")
    today = sections_map.get("Where this shows up today", "")
    tw = words(re.sub(r"^```.*?^```", " ", today, flags=re.M | re.S))
    if total and tw / total > 0.20:
        err(loc, f"'Where this shows up today' is {tw}/{total} = {tw/total:.0%} (> 20%)")
    elif total and tw / total > 0.155:
        warn(loc, f"'Where this shows up today' is {tw/total:.0%} of prose")
    if "As of November 2026" not in today:
        err(loc, "'Where this shows up today' lacks an 'As of November 2026' statement")
    for ch in body:
        if unicodedata.category(ch) in ("Mn", "Me", "Cf", "Co", "Cs") and ord(ch) != 0xFE0F:
            err(loc, f"literal combining/format character U+{ord(ch):04X} in body; write an escape")
            break
    if re.search(r"\b(and so on|similar for the rest|TODO|TBD|lorem)\b", body, flags=re.I):
        err(loc, "placeholder wording in body")


def question_checks(loc, s, fm):
    qs = fm.get("questions") or []
    if not 5 <= len(qs) <= 7:
        err(loc, f"{len(qs)} questions (want 5-7)")
    seen = set()
    positions = Counter()
    first_positions = Counter()
    total_correct = 0
    longest = 0
    singles = 0
    for k, q in enumerate(qs, start=1):
        ql = f"{loc} q{k}"
        for key in ("id", "prompt", "type", "explanation", "options"):
            if key not in q:
                err(ql, f"missing {key}")
        qid = q.get("id")
        if not isinstance(qid, str) or not SLUG.match(qid):
            err(ql, f"bad id {qid!r}")
        elif qid.lower() in RESERVED_IDS:
            err(ql, f"reserved id {qid!r}")
        if qid in seen:
            err(ql, f"duplicate id {qid}")
        seen.add(qid)
        prompt = q.get("prompt", "")
        if not isinstance(prompt, str) or not prompt.strip():
            err(ql, "empty prompt")
        expl = q.get("explanation", "")
        if not isinstance(expl, str) or len(expl.strip()) < 200:
            err(ql, "explanation missing or too short")
        if re.search(r"\b[Oo]ption\s+[A-Ea-e1-5]\b|\b(first|second|third|fourth|fifth|last|top|bottom)\s+option\b|(?:^|\s)\(\s*[a-eA-E]\s*\)", expl or "", flags=re.M):
            err(ql, "explanation refers to options by letter/position")
        low = (prompt + " " + " ".join(o.get("text", "") for o in q.get("options", []))).lower()
        if "all of the above" in low or "none of the above" in low:
            err(ql, "all/none of the above")
        if re.search(r"\bnot\b", prompt) and "**NOT**" not in prompt:
            warn(ql, "negation in stem without **NOT** emphasis")
        opts = q.get("options") or []
        for o in opts:
            if set(o) - {"text", "correct"}:
                err(ql, f"unexpected option keys {set(o)}")
            if "correct" in o and o["correct"] is not True:
                err(ql, "correct key present but not true")
            if not isinstance(o.get("text"), str) or not o["text"].strip():
                err(ql, "option without text")
        texts = [o.get("text", "") for o in opts]
        if len(set(texts)) != len(texts):
            err(ql, "duplicate option text")
        correct_idx = [i for i, o in enumerate(opts) if o.get("correct") is True]
        n = len(opts)
        t = q.get("type")
        if t == "single":
            singles += 1
            stats["single"] += 1
            if len(correct_idx) != 1:
                err(ql, f"single with {len(correct_idx)} correct")
            if not 4 <= n <= 5:
                err(ql, f"single with {n} options")
            if correct_idx:
                lens = [len(x) for x in texts]
                c = correct_idx[0]
                if lens[c] == max(lens) and lens.count(max(lens)) == 1:
                    longest += 1
        elif t == "multiple":
            stats["multiple"] += 1
            if not 2 <= len(correct_idx) <= 3:
                err(ql, f"multiple with {len(correct_idx)} correct")
            if n != 5:
                err(ql, f"multiple with {n} options (want 5)")
            if not prompt.rstrip().endswith("Select all that apply."):
                err(ql, "multiple prompt must end with 'Select all that apply.'")
        else:
            err(ql, f"bad type {t!r}")
        if n and correct_idx:
            first = (k + s) % n
            expected = sorted((first + j) % n for j in range(len(correct_idx)))
            if sorted(correct_idx) != expected:
                err(ql, f"correct positions {correct_idx} != expected {expected} (k={k}, s={s}, n={n})")
            first_positions[first] += 1
            for i in correct_idx:
                positions[i] += 1
                total_correct += 1
    for name, counter, tot in (("all-correct", positions, total_correct), ("first-correct", first_positions, len(qs))):
        if tot and max(counter.values()) / tot > 0.40:
            err(loc, f"{name} position concentration {dict(counter)} exceeds 40%")
    if singles and longest / singles > 0.5:
        err(loc, f"correct option is the unique longest in {longest}/{singles} single questions")
    longest_correct[0] += longest
    longest_correct[1] += singles
    stats["questions"] += len(qs)


def compiler_port(loc, fm):
    title = fm.get("title")
    if not isinstance(title, str) or not title.strip():
        err(loc, "[compiler] title is required")
    if fm.get("draft"):
        err(loc, "[compiler] draft subchapter")
    seen = set()
    for i, q in enumerate(fm.get("questions") or []):
        qid = (q.get("id") or "").strip() or f"q{i+1}"
        if not SLUG.match(qid):
            err(loc, f"[compiler] question '{qid}' id invalid")
            continue
        if qid in seen:
            err(loc, f"[compiler] duplicate question id {qid}")
        seen.add(qid)
        if not str(q.get("prompt") or "").strip():
            err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} prompt is required")
        opts = q.get("options") or []
        oseen = set()
        for j, o in enumerate(opts):
            oid = (o.get("id") or "").strip() or (chr(97 + j) if j < 26 else f"o{j+1}")
            if not SLUG.match(oid) or oid in oseen:
                err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} option id {oid} invalid/duplicate")
            oseen.add(oid)
            if not str(o.get("text") or "").strip():
                err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} option {oid} has no text")
            if "correct" in o and not isinstance(o["correct"], bool):
                err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} correct is not a boolean")
        cc = sum(1 for o in opts if o.get("correct") is True)
        if len(opts) < 2:
            err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} at least 2 options are required")
        if cc == 0:
            err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} at least one option must be marked correct")
        t = q.get("type")
        if t is not None:
            if not isinstance(t, str):
                err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} type not a string")
            else:
                nt = t.strip().lower()
                if nt not in ("", "single", "multiple"):
                    err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} unknown type {t}")
                if nt == "single" and cc > 1:
                    err(loc, f"[compiler] {qid} single but >1 correct")


def main():
    check_book()
    chs = chapters()
    for order, slug, cdir in chs:
        if order < 0:
            err(rel(cdir), "[compiler] name must look like '01-my-slug'")
        check_chapter(cdir)
        for f in os.listdir(cdir):
            if f == "chapter.yml" or hidden(f):
                continue
            if not f.endswith(".md"):
                err(rel(os.path.join(cdir, f)), "unexpected file")
            elif not NUMBERED.match(f[:-3]):
                err(rel(os.path.join(cdir, f)), "[compiler] bad section file name")
    for s, (cdir, path) in enumerate(sections(), start=1):
        loc = rel(path)
        stats["sections"] += 1
        raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        yb, body = split_front_matter(raw)
        if yb is None:
            err(loc, "no front matter")
            continue
        raw_quote_checks(loc, yb)
        try:
            fm = yaml.safe_load(yb)
        except yaml.YAMLError as e:
            err(loc, f"[compiler] invalid front matter: {e}")
            continue
        compiler_port(loc, fm)
        question_checks(loc, s, fm)
        body_checks(loc, body)
    if longest_correct[1] and longest_correct[0] / longest_correct[1] > 0.40:
        err("book", f"correct option is unique-longest in {longest_correct[0]}/{longest_correct[1]} singles")
    print(f"chapters={len(chs)} sections={stats['sections']} questions={stats['questions']} "
          f"single={stats['single']} multiple={stats['multiple']} "
          f"correct-is-longest={longest_correct[0]}/{longest_correct[1]}")
    if stats["words"]:
        print(f"prose words: min={min(stats['words'])} max={max(stats['words'])} total={sum(stats['words'])}")
    for w in warnings:
        print("WARNING:", w)
    for e in errors:
        print("ERROR:", e)
    print(f"{len(errors)} error(s), {len(warnings)} warning(s)")
    return 1 if errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# NOTES — networking-and-protocols

Running log of decisions, rule sources and conflicts. Unattended run, 2026-11-27.

## Environment

- No local checkout existed. `dump.txt` (project doc, export 2026-11-27T22:09Z) was read first, then the
  public repository was cloned (`git clone --depth 1`, HEAD e3d5f37, 2026-11-27 17:10 -0500) to read the
  existing books that the dump only inventories.
- No .NET SDK in the sandbox; the egress proxy refuses builds.dotnet.microsoft.com and api.nuget.org
  (HTTP 403 on CONNECT), so the real ContentProcessor cannot be built or run. As in the
  relational-sql-and-transactions and data-representation-traps runs, the compiler's rules are ported
  into `validate.py` and checked with PyYAML 6.0.3. Logged as unresolved in REPORT.md.
- curl to www.rfc-editor.org is refused by the proxy, but the WebFetch/WebSearch tools reach
  rfc-editor.org, datatracker.ietf.org and vendor sites. RFC status was checked there (see "RFC audit").
- The PAT in the user's preferences was not needed (anonymous clone worked; no GitHub API use).

## Compiler rules (source wins)

Re-read from `tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor` in the dump; unchanged from the previous runs:

- Book slug `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`; chapter folders and section files `^(\d+)[-_](slug)$`;
  names starting with `.` or `_` are hidden.
- `book.yml`: title (required), author, summary, date, updated, tags, image, draft. Future dates skipped.
- `chapter.yml`: title (required), summary, draft.
- Section front matter starts at byte 0 with `---` and ends at the first `\n---`; YamlDotNet with
  camelCase and IgnoreUnmatchedProperties (unknown keys silently ignored, so validate.py rejects them).
- Question: id optional (slug regex, unique), prompt required, type null/single/multiple (single with
  more than one correct is an error), options >= 2, at least one `correct` (YAML bool), option text required.
- SyntaxHighlighter: csharp, javascript, typescript, python, sql, bash, json, yaml, html (xml), css plus
  aliases. Intersection with the prompt's allow-list: csharp, python, javascript, sql, bash, json, yaml, html.
  This book uses `bash` (raw HTTP, DNS output, packet traces), `python` and `csharp`.
- Block scalars (`explanation: |-`): standard YAML and supported by YamlDotNet. The
  relational-sql-and-transactions book is merged on main (deploy.yml and pr-check.yml both run the content
  processor, which fails the build on bad YAML) and uses `|-` in every question. The CI result itself could
  not be inspected from the sandbox (GitHub API use was denied), so acceptance is inferred, not observed.
  Decision: use `|-`.

## Style decisions copied from existing books

- Author id `terlingua-team` (exists in content/authors; most common in book.yml files).
- Date: unquoted `2026-11-27` (DateTime). `draft: false` and `correct: true` unquoted (bools).
- Title/summary/tags double-quoted like relational-sql-and-transactions.
- Section bodies end with a `## Sources` heading after the six required headings (house style of the two
  most recent books). Conflict with "exact six headings" logged below.

## Authoring pipeline

- Sources in `_build/networking-and-protocols/src/NN-chapter/NN-section.md` with per-question `correct:`
  and `distractors:` lists and `checks:` (Python statements, run by check_math.py). `chapter.yml` and
  `book.yml` are written directly into content/.
- `build.py` emits the content files: every string double-quoted (JSON escaping), explanations as `|-`,
  options placed by the position rule: first correct at (k + s) mod n, further correct options at the
  next indexes modulo n, distractors in authored order in the remaining slots.

## RFC audit (status checked 2026-11-27 on rfc-editor.org / datatracker)

- RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) is OBSOLETED by RFC 9846 (July 2026). The book cites RFC 9846 as the TLS 1.3
  specification and mentions RFC 8446 as the original 2018 version. This is a conflict with the prompt's
  source list; the RFC Editor wins.
- RFC 8312 (CUBIC) obsoleted by RFC 9438 (Proposed Standard, 2023), which updates RFC 5681.
- Current (no "obsoleted by"): 791 (STD 5), 8200 (STD 86, updated by 9673), 4632 (BCP 122), 826 (STD 37),
  4861 (updated by many), 1191, 8201 (STD 87), 9293 (STD 7), 5681 (updated by 9438), 6298,
  9000/9001/9002, 9114, 9110 (STD 97), 9111 (STD 98), 9112 (STD 99, updated by 9931), 9113,
  1034/1035 (STD 13), 2181, 2308, 5280 (updated by several), 6455 (updated by 7936, 8307, 8441),
  9460 (SVCB/HTTPS), 8484 (DoH).
- New RFCs found: RFC 9849 (ECH, March 2026), RFC 9848 (ECH bootstrapping via SVCB), RFC 10024 (hybrid
  ECDHE-MLKEM for TLS 1.3; X25519MLKEM768 codepoint 0x11EC, client share 1216 bytes).
- Section numbers are cited only where the fetched text confirmed them: RFC 2308 §5 (negative TTL =
  min(SOA MINIMUM, SOA TTL)), RFC 2181 §10.1 (CNAME and other data), §10.3 (MX/NS not aliases), §8
  (TTL range), RFC 9111 §5.2.2.4 (no-cache), §5.2.2.2 (must-revalidate), RFC 4632 §5.1 (longest match),
  RFC 9112 §9.3.2 (pipelining order), RFC 8200 §5 (1280 minimum MTU), RFC 9113 §5.3.2 (RFC 7540 priorities
  deprecated). Everything else is cited at RFC-number level.

## Dated claims verified (sources)

- Google IPv6 statistics first exceeded 50% on 28 March 2026 (Internet Society Pulse; APNIC blog
  2026-04-28 also gives APNIC Labs ~42% capability).
- CUBIC default in Linux, Windows and Apple stacks: stated in RFC 9438 itself. BBR: draft-ietf-ccwg-bbr-06
  (July 2026) specifies BBRv3, intended status Experimental, not an RFC.
- HTTP/3 enabled by default: Chrome/Edge 87, Firefox 88, Safari 18 (web-platform-dx web-features data,
  Baseline low date 2024-09-16).
- CA/Browser Forum ballot SC-081v3 (April 2025): max TLS cert validity 200 days from 2026-03-15, 100 days
  from 2027-03-15, 47 days from 2029-03-15; DCV reuse down to 10 days in 2029.
- Let's Encrypt: 90-day default, 6-day short-lived profile optional; 64 days from 2027-02-10, 45 days from
  2028-02-16 (letsencrypt.org upcoming features / cert-lifetimes pages, updated July 2026); its
  certificates carry a CRL distribution point instead of an OCSP URL.
- X25519MLKEM768 default: Chrome 131+, Firefox 132+ (desktop), Safari 26+ (Cloudflare PQC support doc).
- Idempotency-Key header: draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-09 (21 November 2026), WG document,
  not an RFC.

## Conflicts and resolutions

1. Prompt "run the repo's real build" vs no SDK/NuGet access -> ported validation (above).
2. Prompt "double-quote every string" vs YAML dates/bools -> dates and bools unquoted.
3. Six required headings vs house `## Sources` -> Sources appended last.
4. RFC 8446 in the prompt's source list is obsolete -> RFC 9846 cited (see RFC audit).
5. "Next valid index(es)" for multiple questions interpreted as wrapping modulo n (same as previous runs).
6. RFC 5861 (stale-while-revalidate) is Informational, not part of RFC 9111; described as such.
7. TIME_WAIT on Linux (60 s), Linux minimum RTO (200 ms), delayed-ACK minimum (~40 ms) and Linux's initial
   window of 10 are stated as long-standing implementation values, not as "As of" claims; the TIME_WAIT
   constant was checked against kernel-source discussions found by search, the others were not re-verified.
8. Prompt rule "dated facts must never be the only reason an answer is correct": the one question built on
   a dated schedule (s21 `max-validity-date`) states the SC-081 schedule in its prompt, so the answer is
   derivable from the prompt plus arithmetic.
9. Ch7 (review) has 3 sections; total 30 sections (within 25–32).

- Position rule: 13 single-answer questions received a fifth, misconception-based distractor (addopt.py)

  after shortening 29 correct options and lengthening 12 distractors (relen.py, relen2.py). Explanations
  quote distractors by prefix, so appended words did not break them.

## Validation output (validate.py)

```
stats: {'chapters': 7, 'sections': 30, 'questions': 180, 'type_single': 150, 'type_multiple': 30, 'longest_correct': 51, 'prose_words': 16093}
correct-answer positions (book): {0: 49, 1: 48, 2: 48, 3: 53, 4: 20}
0 error(s), 0 warning(s)
```

validate.py ports the compiler's rules (naming regexes, front-matter split on `\n---`, YAML keys, question
and option rules) and checks the prompt's hard rules: every string double-quoted, `type` always present,
4–5 options (5 for multiple, 2–3 correct), "Select all that apply." placement, reserved ids, no option
references by letter or position, no all/none of the above, code-fence languages, heading order and bullet
counts, 400–1200 prose words, the size of the "today" block and its "As of November 2026" claim, the
(k + s) mod n position rule and the 40% per-position cap. All front matter also parses with ruamel.yaml
(YAML 1.2, pure Python) as a second parser.

## Math audit (check_math.py)

```
checks: 183 run, 0 failed, 30 source files
```

Every CIDR boundary, host count, summary and longest-prefix match (Python `ipaddress`), MTU/MSS and fragment
offset, sequence/ACK number, RTO update, slow-start round count, BDP, window, Mathis estimate, NAT and
TIME_WAIT port arithmetic, TLS record count and nonce, WebSocket accept value, cache age, date arithmetic
and latency total used in an option, explanation or worked example has a `checks:` or `body_checks:` entry.
The audit caught one real error during writing (a mistyped WebSocket GUID in the helper), fixed against the
RFC's own example.

## RFC audit

All cited RFCs were looked up on rfc-editor.org or datatracker (see NOTES.md). Findings that changed the book:

- RFC 8446 is obsolete: TLS 1.3 is now RFC 9846 (July 2026). The book cites RFC 9846 throughout and mentions
  RFC 8446 as the original version.
- RFC 8312 (CUBIC) is obsolete: RFC 9438 is cited.
- New RFCs used: RFC 9849 (ECH, March 2026), RFC 9848 (ECH via SVCB), RFC 10024 (hybrid ECDHE-MLKEM),
  RFC 9525 (service identity, obsoletes RFC 6125).
- Section numbers appear only where they were confirmed in the fetched RFC text (list in NOTES.md).

## Question audit

All 180 questions were re-read against their explanations. `audit.py` adds a structural check (one quoted
rebuttal per distractor); its 7 flags were reviewed by hand and are explanations that rebut distractors in
bullets or combined sentences without quoting them (for example, 301 and 302 handled together). Fixes made
during the audit: a misleading statement about where the child's SOA appears (s15), the stale-while-
revalidate explanation now rebuts each distractor separately (s25), a rounding inconsistency in the Mathis
question (s29), escaped quotes inside block scalars (s11, s26), and the option-length and position
rebalancing described in NOTES.md.

## Unresolved items and uncertainties

1. **Real compiler not run.** No .NET SDK in the sandbox, and dot.net / nuget.org are blocked by the egress
   proxy. Please run `dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor` (or `dotnet test`) once
   before merging. Residual risk is low: the format matches the merged relational-sql-and-transactions book
   (block-scalar explanations, quoted strings), and two independent YAML parsers accept every file.
2. **C# snippets not compiled** (s10, s23, s30). Python snippets in s11, s20, s26 and s27 were executed.
3. **Illustrative command output.** tcpdump, ss, dig, openssl and curl outputs use documentation addresses and
   are abridged; the DNSSEC and 0-RTT outputs are labeled illustrative in the text. They show formats and
   relationships, not captures from real hosts.
4. **Implementation constants** stated without an "As of" date and not re-verified this run: Linux TIME_WAIT
   60 s (checked only against kernel-source discussions), Linux minimum RTO 200 ms, delayed-ACK ≈ 40 ms,
   initial window 10, Go and Kestrel enabling `TCP_NODELAY` by default.
5. **Dated claims** were each checked against a primary or vendor source on 2026-11-27 (list in NOTES.md).
   Two depend on secondary aggregation: browser HTTP/3 defaults (web-platform-dx web-features data) and
   browser hybrid post-quantum defaults (Cloudflare's PQC support page). No adoption percentage is given
   except Google's IPv6 crossing 50% on 28 March 2026 and APNIC's ~42% (April 2026), both attributed.
6. **RFC 6585 §4, RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5 and §6, RFC 7838 `ma` default** are cited from the documents' known
   structure; their current status was not re-fetched in this run.
7. **Timeless-question limit** (at most one dated question per section) was applied by hand. The only
   question resting on a dated schedule (s21) states the schedule in its prompt.
8. **House style addition:** each section ends with `## Sources` after the six required headings, as in the
   existing books; remove it if the exact six-heading structure is required.

==> _build/networking-and-protocols/addopt.py <==
import pathlib, sys, yaml
SRC = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "src"
def add(rel, qid, distractor, expl):
    p = next(SRC.glob(rel))
    s = p.read_text()
    i = s.index(f'  - id: "{qid}"')
    j = s.find('\n  - id: "', i + 1)
    if j < 0: j = s.index('\n---', i)
    block = s[i:j]
    k = block.index('    explanation: |-')
    d = block.index('    distractors:\n')
    dl = block[d:k]
    new_dl = dl.rstrip('\n') + '\n      - ' + __import__('json').dumps(distractor, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n'
    block = block[:d] + new_dl + block[k:]
    # append explanation paragraph at end of explanation scalar (before checks: or end)
    e = block.index('    explanation: |-')
    c = block.find('\n    checks:', e)
    end = c if c >= 0 else len(block.rstrip('\n'))
    block = block[:end] + '\n\n      ' + expl + block[end:]
    s = s[:i] + block + s[j:]
    p.write_text(s)
    yaml.safe_load(s[3:s.index('\n---', 3)])

 ("02-*/01-*.md","flow-byte-count-bug","Delayed ACKs acknowledge two extra sequence numbers so that the sender can detect the end of the stream","\"Delayed ACKs acknowledge two extra numbers\" invents a rule: delaying an ACK changes when it is sent, never the number it carries."),
 ("02-*/02-*.md","who-gets-time-wait","The client, because it sent the final ACK of the opening handshake",'"Sent the final ACK of the opening handshake" mixes up connection setup with teardown; TIME-WAIT belongs to whoever sends the first FIN.'),

 ("06-*/02-*.md","post-redirect-303","`GET /orders`, the URL of the original form",'"`GET /orders`, the original URL" ignores the `Location` header, which names the resource to fetch next.'),

==> _build/networking-and-protocols/audit.py <==
"""Heuristic question audit: every distractor should be discussed in the explanation (quoted prefix),
explanations must not cite options by letter/position, prompts of multiple questions end correctly."""
import pathlib, re, yaml
miss = 0
for f in sorted(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.glob('src/*/*.md')):
    s = f.read_text(); m = yaml.safe_load(s[3:s.index('\n---', 3)])
    for q in m['questions']:
        ex = q['explanation']
        quoted = re.findall(r'"([^"\n]{1,200})"', ex)
        norm = lambda t: re.sub(r'[`*]', '', t).lower().strip()
        for d in q['distractors']:
            nd = norm(d)
            ok = any(len(norm(x).rstrip('.…, ').strip()) >= 1 and norm(x).rstrip('.…, ').strip() in nd for x in quoted)
            if not ok:
                miss += 1
                print(f"{f.parent.name[:2]}/{f.name[:2]} {q['id']}: distractor not quoted: {d[:70]}")
print("unquoted distractors:", miss)

print("--- structural check: one quoted rebuttal per distractor ---")
bad = 0
for f in sorted(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.glob('src/*/*.md')):
    s = f.read_text(); m = yaml.safe_load(s[3:s.index('\n---', 3)])
    for q in m['questions']:
        reb = [l for l in q['explanation'].splitlines() if re.match(r'^\s*(- )?(\*\*)?"', l)]
        if len(reb) < len(q['distractors']):
            bad += 1
            print(f"{f.parent.name[:2]}/{f.name[:2]} {q['id']}: {len(reb)} rebuttals for {len(q['distractors'])} distractors")
print("questions with fewer rebuttals than distractors:", bad)

import sys, pathlib, yaml, collections, itertools
SRC = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "src"
files = [f for ch in sorted(p for p in SRC.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) for f in sorted(ch.glob("*.md"))]
def dist(qs, s, ns):
    c = collections.Counter()
    for k, (q, n) in enumerate(zip(qs, ns), start=1):
        first = (k + s) % n
        for j in range(len(q["correct"])): c[(first + j) % n] += 1
    return c
for s, f in enumerate(files, start=1):
    raw = f.read_text(); meta = yaml.safe_load(raw[3:raw.index("\n---", 3)])
    qs = meta["questions"]; ns = [len(q["correct"]) + len(q["distractors"]) for q in qs]
    c = dist(qs, s, ns); tot = sum(c.values()); top = max(c.values())
    if top / tot > 0.40:
        fixes = []
        for k, q in enumerate(qs):
            if q["type"] == "single":
                for newn in (4, 5):
                    if newn != ns[k]:
                        ns2 = list(ns); ns2[k] = newn; c2 = dist(qs, s, ns2)
                        if max(c2.values()) / sum(c2.values()) <= 0.40: fixes.append((k + 1, q["id"], newn))
        print(f"s{s} {f.name}: {dict(c)} fixes: {fixes}")

==> _build/networking-and-protocols/build.py <==
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Emit content/books/networking-and-protocols section files from _build sources.

Source files: _build/networking-and-protocols/src/NN-chapter/NN-section.md
Front matter keys per question: id, type, prompt, explanation, correct (list), distractors (list),
checks (list, used only by check_sql.py). Options are placed by the answer-position rule:
first correct option at index (k + s) mod n, further correct options at the next indexes (mod n).
"""
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import yaml

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BUILD = ROOT / "_build" / "networking-and-protocols"
SRC = BUILD / "src"
OUT = ROOT / "content" / "books" / "networking-and-protocols"


def split_front_matter(raw: str):
    if not raw.startswith("---"):
        raise ValueError("missing front matter")
    end = raw.index("\n---", 3)
    return raw[3:end].strip(), raw[end + 4:].lstrip("\r\n")


def q(s: str) -> str:
    return json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)


def section_sources():
    files = []
    for chapter in sorted(p for p in SRC.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        for f in sorted(chapter.glob("*.md")):
            files.append(f)
    return files


def place(correct, distractors, k, s):
    n = len(correct) + len(distractors)
    first = (k + s) % n
    slots = [None] * n
    for j, text in enumerate(correct):
        slots[(first + j) % n] = (text, True)
    it = iter(distractors)
    for i in range(n):
        if slots[i] is None:
            slots[i] = (next(it), False)
    return slots


def render(meta, body, s):
    lines = ["---", f"title: {q(meta['title'])}", "questions:"]
    for k, question in enumerate(meta["questions"], start=1):
        lines.append(f"  - id: {q(question['id'])}")
        lines.append(f"    type: {q(question['type'])}")
        lines.append(f"    prompt: {q(question['prompt'].strip())}")
        lines.append("    explanation: |-")
        for line in question["explanation"].strip("\n").split("\n"):
            lines.append(("      " + line) if line.strip() else "")
        lines.append("    options:")
        for text, correct in place(question["correct"], question["distractors"], k, s):
            lines.append(f"      - text: {q(text)}")
            if correct:
                lines.append("        correct: true")
    lines.append("---")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"


def main():
    sources = section_sources()
    written = 0
    for s, src in enumerate(sources, start=1):
        fm, body = split_front_matter(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        meta = yaml.safe_load(fm)
        out = OUT / src.parent.name / src.name
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(render(meta, body, s), encoding="utf-8")
        written += 1
    print(f"built {written} section file(s)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

==> _build/networking-and-protocols/check_math.py <==
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recompute every number used in the book.

Each source file under src/ may carry `body_checks:` (front matter, for figures in the prose and worked
example) and per-question `checks:`. Both are lists of Python statements, usually `assert` lines, run in a
namespace with ipaddress, math, hashlib, base64 and the helpers below. A failing assert is reported with
its location."""
import base64
import hashlib
import ipaddress
import math
import pathlib
import sys

import yaml

SRC = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "src"


def net(cidr):
    return ipaddress.ip_network(cidr, strict=False)


def lpm(addr, routes):
    a = ipaddress.ip_address(addr)
    best = None
    for r in routes:
        n = ipaddress.ip_network(r)
        if a in n and (best is None or n.prefixlen > best.prefixlen):
            best = n
    return str(best)


def usable_hosts(cidr):
    n = ipaddress.ip_network(cidr)
    if n.version == 4 and n.prefixlen <= 30:
        return n.num_addresses - 2
    return n.num_addresses


def summarize(cidrs):
    return [str(x) for x in ipaddress.collapse_addresses(ipaddress.ip_network(c) for c in cidrs)]


def rto_update(srtt, rttvar, r, alpha=1 / 8, beta=1 / 4, g=0.0, k=4, min_rto=1.0):
    rttvar = (1 - beta) * rttvar + beta * abs(srtt - r)
    srtt = (1 - alpha) * srtt + alpha * r
    return srtt, rttvar, max(min_rto, srtt + max(g, k * rttvar))


def slow_start_rtts(iw, target):
    cwnd, rtts = iw, 0
    while cwnd < target:
        cwnd *= 2
        rtts += 1
    return rtts


def ws_accept(key):
    guid = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11"
    return base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha1((key + guid).encode()).digest()).decode()


def close(a, b, tol=1e-6):
    return abs(a - b) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(a), abs(b))


def main():
    files = [f for ch in sorted(p for p in SRC.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) for f in sorted(ch.glob("*.md"))]
    total, failures = 0, []
    for f in files:
        raw = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        meta = yaml.safe_load(raw[3:raw.index("\n---", 3)])
        blocks = [("body", c) for c in meta.get("body_checks") or []]
        for q in meta.get("questions") or []:
            blocks += [(q["id"], c) for c in q.get("checks") or []]
        for loc, code in blocks:
            total += 1
            ns = dict(ipaddress=ipaddress, math=math, hashlib=hashlib, base64=base64, net=net, lpm=lpm,
                      usable_hosts=usable_hosts, summarize=summarize, rto_update=rto_update,
                      slow_start_rtts=slow_start_rtts, ws_accept=ws_accept, close=close)
            try:
                exec(code, ns)
            except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
                failures.append(f"{f.parent.name}/{f.name} [{loc}]: {type(ex).__name__}: {ex}\n    {code.strip()}")
    for x in failures:
        print("FAIL:", x)
    print(f"checks: {total} run, {len(failures)} failed, {len(files)} source files")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Plan — Networking & Internet Protocols: RFC Mechanics

7 chapters, 30 sections, 6 questions per section (180 total). s = book-wide section number.

## 01-layering-addressing-and-routing — "Layering, Addressing and Routing"

| s | File | Goal | Question concepts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 01-layers-and-the-hourglass.md | Use OSI as a vocabulary and TCP/IP as the real architecture; compute encapsulation overhead | narrow waist (IP) meaning; encapsulation order on the wire; header-overhead efficiency arithmetic; which layer a device examines (switch/router/L4 LB); end-to-end principle; frames per payload count |
| 2 | 02-mac-ip-arp-and-ndp.md | Trace which addresses change per hop; resolve next hops with ARP/NDP | MAC rewritten per hop, IP unchanged; host ARPs for gateway not remote IP; ARP request broadcast vs reply unicast; IPv6 solicited-node multicast address computation; stale ARP / duplicate IP after failover (gratuitous ARP); TTL/hop-limit decrement trace |
| 3 | 03-cidr-subnets-and-longest-prefix-match.md | Do CIDR arithmetic and pick routes by longest prefix | network/broadcast of an address; usable host count (/31 /32 special); summarization of contiguous blocks; longest-prefix match among routes; "is X in subnet Y" bug with string prefix; IPv6 /64 and /48 counts |
| 4 | 04-nat-and-port-exhaustion.md | Explain NAPT mappings and compute port exhaustion | NAPT rewrites src addr+port and reverse; unsolicited inbound dropped; ports per (dst ip, dst port) arithmetic; connection pool / many destinations to mitigate; RFC 1918 vs RFC 6598 shared space; IPv6 adoption (dated) |

import pathlib, json, sys
SRC = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "src"
def opt(glob, old, new):
    p = next(SRC.glob(glob)); s = p.read_text()
    a = "- " + json.dumps(old, ensure_ascii=False); b = "- " + json.dumps(new, ensure_ascii=False)
    if s.count(a) != 1: print("NOT FOUND/AMBIG", glob, old[:50]); return
    p.write_text(s.replace(a, b))
